name: Mobile-Tensaw River Delta
blurb: Cypress swamp, shad and gar, and the alligators that keep nutria and hogs in check.

tip.title: Remove the alligators
tip.text: Alligators eat nutria and feral pigs. Set American alligator to -100% and watch nutria, then the cypress seedlings and marsh grass they eat.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Seasonal river flooding
nodes.desc: Spring and winter floods from the Mobile and Tensaw rivers spread water, silt and seeds across the bottomland forest and swamp.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light drives algae in open water and growth in the marsh and forest canopy.

nodes.name: River sediment & nutrients
nodes.desc: The rivers drain much of Alabama and deliver silt and nutrients that build the delta soils.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead leaves, wood and animals in the swamp and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Bald cypress
nodes.desc: A swamp conifer that tolerates flooding. Squirrels eat its seeds, and floodwater spreads them along streams.

nodes.name: Bottomland oaks
nodes.desc: Oaks in the floodplain forest drop acorns, a food for squirrels and feral pigs.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae in the delta channels and bays that feed small filter-feeding fish.

nodes.name: Smooth cordgrass
nodes.desc: A grass of the tidal brackish marshes at the lower delta, where fresh and salt water meet.

nodes.name: Beggarticks
nodes.desc: A common wildflower of open ground. GloBI records it as food for the eastern lubber grasshopper.

nodes.name: Eastern gray squirrel
nodes.desc: Eats seeds and nuts, including cypress seeds and acorns, and often drops cone scales still holding seeds.

nodes.name: Nutria
nodes.desc: An invasive rodent that clips and uproots young cypress seedlings and damages coastal marshes.

nodes.name: Gizzard shad
nodes.desc: A schooling fish that strains algae and organic bits from the water. It is a main prey for larger fish and fish-eating birds.

nodes.name: Blue crab
nodes.desc: An omnivore of brackish and tidal waters in the lower delta. Brackish alligator gar feed heavily on it.

nodes.name: Eastern lubber grasshopper
nodes.desc: A large, slow grasshopper that eats broadleaf plants such as beggarticks.

nodes.name: Green frog
nodes.desc: A pond and swamp-edge frog eaten by water snakes and herons.

nodes.name: Feral pig
nodes.desc: An invasive omnivore that eats plants and animals such as small mammals, birds, turtles, snakes and amphibians. A major threat to the delta.

nodes.name: Banded water snake
nodes.desc: A common water snake that eats frogs and toads.

nodes.name: Cottonmouth
nodes.desc: A venomous swamp snake that eats other snakes, among other prey.

nodes.name: Alligator gar
nodes.desc: An ambush predator of slow river backwaters and brackish marsh. Eats mainly shad and other fish, and blue crabs in brackish water.

nodes.name: Great blue heron
nodes.desc: Wades in shallows and spears fish, frogs and snakes.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: Almost entirely a fish eater. It plunges feet first onto prey from the air.

nodes.name: American alligator
nodes.desc: An opportunistic top predator that eats fish, crustaceans, reptiles, birds and mammals, including nutria and feral pigs. Its dug holes shelter other animals in dry spells.
